title: podman cp ignores named-volume subpath for created and stopped containers
body:
### Environment

Podman 6.1.2 (Alvistack/OBS package), Debian 13 Linux amd64, rootless,
crun 1.30, overlay storage with fuse-overlayfs. Reproduction uses Podman CLI
directly, without Compose or OURS.

### Minimal reproduction

```sh
set -eu
volume="cp-subpath-repro-$$"
container="cp-subpath-repro-$$"
out=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
  podman rm -f "$container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  podman volume rm "$volume" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$out"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

podman volume create "$volume"
podman run --rm --network=none \
  --mount "type=volume,source=$volume,target=/data" \
  docker.io/library/node:24 sh -c \
  'mkdir -p /data/sub; echo ROOT_MARKER > /data/probe; echo SUBPATH_MARKER > /data/sub/probe'
podman create --name "$container" --network=none \
  --mount "type=volume,source=$volume,target=/data,subpath=sub" \
  docker.io/library/node:24 sleep 120

podman cp "$container:/data/probe" "$out/created"
podman start "$container"
podman exec "$container" cat /data/probe
podman cp "$container:/data/probe" "$out/running"
podman stop -t 1 "$container"
podman cp "$container:/data/probe" "$out/stopped"
cat "$out/created" "$out/running" "$out/stopped"
```

Expected: all three copies contain `SUBPATH_MARKER`.

Observed:

```text
ROOT_MARKER
SUBPATH_MARKER
ROOT_MARKER
```

Removing the root-level `probe` turns the wrong-content result into an ENOENT
failure, even though `sub/probe` exists. A control using the whole volume works
in all three states.

### Root cause

The running path uses the container mount namespace. The non-running path calls
`resolvePath`. In
[`container_path_resolution.go`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/v6.1.2/libpod/container_path_resolution.go#L53),
the named-volume case combines `Volume.MountPoint()` directly with the relative
container path; it does not incorporate the selected mount's `SubPath`.
Consequently, the host-side path is rooted at the entire volume.

### Proposed fix

Retain the matching named-volume mount entry and resolve its configured
subpath securely before resolving the relative file path. Preserve traversal
and symlink containment. Add created/stopped/running regression coverage with
different marker files at the volume root and subpath, including a missing root
file. The copy must use the same view the container sees.

[PR #29420](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29420) concerns
per-entry volume resolution when copying archives *into* stopped containers;
this reproduction copies *out* of an explicitly selected subpath and identifies
a separate missing-subpath step in `resolvePath`.

### Additional environment details

Podman runs directly on the Linux host, not inside a container. Rootless. Tested release: 6.1.2.

comments.body:
/assign

Hello, I'd like to work on this issue.

I'll first reproduce the behavior for created, running, and stopped containers, then trace how podman cp resolves named-volume subpaths and add regression coverage before working on the fix.

I'd like to start implementation once the issue is assigned to me so we avoid duplicate work.

Reproduced on Debian 13's own package, `podman 5.4.2+ds1-2+b2`, rootful — so this reaches everyone on Trixie, not only 6.x from OBS. Same volume layout as above (`probe` = ROOT_MARKER at the root, `sub/probe` = SUBPATH_MARKER), `--mount type=volume,source=spvol,target=/data,subpath=sub`, exit codes taken without a pipe. **The copy-in direction is affected too**, which may matter more for whoever picks this up:

```
## created
  cp OUT rc=0  content=ROOT_MARKER
  cp IN  rc=0  lands at: <volume>/new-created        (root, not sub/)
## running
  cp OUT rc=0  content=SUBPATH_MARKER
  cp IN  rc=0  lands at: <volume>/sub/new-running
## stopped
  cp OUT rc=0  content=ROOT_MARKER
  cp IN  rc=0  lands at: <volume>/new-stopped        (root, not sub/)
```

With the volume shared — container `app` mounting `subpath=app` (created, not started) and container `whole` mounting the entire volume (running), each with its own `config.json` — a copy meant for `app` overwrote `whole`'s file, and `app` never saw it:

```
before: whole sees /data/config.json = ROOT config.json (belongs to whole)
podman cp /tmp/config.json app:/data/config.json  → rc=0
after:  whole sees /data/config.json = new app config
after:  app (now started) sees /data/config.json = app's own config.json
```

Control: Debian 13's `docker.io` 26.1.5 with `--mount type=volume,source=spvol,target=/data,volume-subpath=sub` returned SUBPATH_MARKER and wrote under `sub/` in all three states.

Where the subpath is lost, for whoever takes this: in `libpod/container_path_resolution.go`, `findVolume` matches the destination against `c.config.NamedVolumes` but returns `runtime.GetVolume(vol.Name)`, dropping the `NamedVolume` entry that carries `SubPath`; `resolvePath` then does `securejoin.SecureJoin(volume.MountPoint(), pathRelativeToVolume)`. Returning the entry (or its `SubPath`) and joining `mountPoint/SubPath` first looks like it would cover both directions, since the copy-in path resolves through the same function. Same code at `v5.4.2` and on `main` today. A regression test that copies *in* to a stopped container and reads the file back from inside it after start would catch the write side.

Transcript, and a checker that lists containers with `subpath=` volume mounts that are not running: https://homelabpostmortem.com/2026/09/26/podman-cp-ignores-volume-subpath-when-the-container-is-stopped/
